item.correct_answer: While the coach was explaining the new play, two players slipped back into the locker room, where they had left their water bottles.
error_sites: word introducing the clause "the coach was explaining the new play" (preposition before a clause if "During")
word introducing the clause "they had left their water bottles" (pronoun with no role in its clause if "which")

student_error.During the coach was explaining the new: Uses "During" because it means the same time as "While," not seeing that "during" must be followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.
student_error.While the coach was explaining the new p: Uses "which" because it refers to the locker room, not noticing the clause needs a word meaning "in that place."
student_error.During the coach was explaining the new: Picks connecting words by meaning alone, without checking whether each one can introduce a full clause.

item.explanation: Correct: "While" can introduce a clause with its own subject and verb; "during" is a preposition and needs a noun phrase ("during the meeting"). In "they had left their water bottles" the place is not a subject or object, so the clause needs "where" (or "in which"); "which" leaves it ungrammatical. The option with only the first error breaks the first rule, the option with only the second error breaks the second, and the remaining option breaks both.
item.varied_dimension: subordinating conjunction vs preposition before a clause; relative adverb vs relative pronoun

rated_no.option: During the coach was explaining the new play, two players slipped back into the locker room, where they had left their water bottles.
reasons: 'During the coach was explaining' is a form native grade 7 students don't write and it jars on any reading
'During the coach was explaining' sounds wrong to a native-speaking 7th grader even on a quick read.

rated_no.option: During the coach was explaining the new play, two players slipped back into the locker room, which they had left their water bottles.
reasons: the 'During' + clause opening is plainly ungrammatical to native students, so the option is ruled out
The 'During the coach was' opening jumps out as wrong, so even weak students reject it.
